full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam, J: This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 29-11-2017 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 418 of 2013 allowing the appeal while sending back the suit on remand for amendment of the pleading of the respective parties, which arose out of the judgment and decree dated 30-7-2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogura in Other Suit No.67 of 2009 decreeing the suit. 

 2. Facts for disposal of the civil petition in short are that the Petitioner herein as plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Other Suit No.67 of 2009 impleading the present respondents as defendants for a decree of specific performance of contract for sale of 10 decimals of land and a 3(three) storied building standing thereon as described in the schedule to the plaint before the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogura contending, inter alia, that the defendant Md Samsul Haque articulated publicly in the vicinity to sell the property in question and in this perspective the Plaintiff agreed to purchase the same and, as such, mutual negotiation has been carried out between them, wherein consideration money of the property in question had been settled for an amount of Taka 29,00,000. 

 6. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra, decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 30-7-2013. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, the defendant preferred First Appeal being No.418 of 2013 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing both the sides allowed the appeal on 29-11-2017 by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and sending back the suit on remand for amendment of the respective pleading of the parties. 

 11. Next he submits that having been used no gross of misreading evidence or found on misconception or misapplication or misapprehension of law or of any misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise perverse being contrary to law, the High Court Division in a very cursory, slipshod and cryptic manner allowed the appeal, but over enthusiastically sending back the suit on remand for amendment of the respective pleading of the defendant-parties, giving complete relief to respondent, while the learned trial Court upon hearing both the sides exhaustively and comprehensively decreed the suit and for that reason the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with by this Court. 

 "In Jagesh Chandra Das vs Farida Hasan 1983 BLD (AD) 225 this Court refused to enforce the contract on the ground of hardship when two circumstances were established (a) a very low price (b) contract was performed under compelling circumstances when the members of the minority community were contemplating to migrate from the country. In a similar situation a Division Bench of Karnataka High Court considered the problem in Ranganayakamma vs Gavinda Narayan AIR 1982 (Kant) 264. The facts are exactly on all fours with the present case. There also her husband made a contract for selling his dwelling house and soon thereafter he died, the plaintiff brought the suit for specific performance in 1970. The consideration was Taka 21,000 and advance was paid Taka 3,000. Since the deed of sale was not executed the suit was filed. The defence was mainly on hardship. The Division Bench carefully considered the defence and concluded "If we decree the suit, she will be deprived of that income too, for the rest of her life with no shelter to cover her head. There can, therefore, be no justification for us to tell her that she should sell the house and go on pilgrimage never to return." The Court considered that the plaintiff was a businessman in that case and not a helpless widow like the defendant. In view of those facts, the Court refused to enforce the specific performance no doubt, but appreciated the gesture of the appellant to return the advance amount by three limes. This case shows the judicial anxiety to do justice when faced with the similar situation as emphasised in item-II namely, hardship vs hardship qualified by legal mandate "hardship which he did not foresee vis-a-vis no such hardship would accrue to the plaintiff" Having given our anxious consideration to the facts of this case, we are of the opinion that this contract should, not be enforced specifically if the defendant appellants return the entire advance money of Taka 8,500 with a solatium of Taka 1,00,000 to the plaintiff respondent. In Jagesh Chandra Das's case (Supra) we directed the return of Taka 300paid as advance and compensation of Taka 40,000 to the plaintiff failing which "the plaintiffs suit stands decreed in full." Mr BN Chowdhury, learned Counsel, appearing for the defendant-appellants, in his characteristic manner informed the Court that his client will be bound by any reasonable solatium if pronouncement is made by the Court." 

 "Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act states that granting of a decree for specific performance of contract is a discretion of the court and the same must be exercised not arbitrarily but on the basis of sound and reasonable principles and capable of correction by a Court of appeal. Illustration of Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act speaks that the Court may not exercise the discretion for specific performance of contract where the performance would involve some hardship on the part of the defendant which he did not foresee whereas its non-performance would involve no such hardship on the plaintiff. It was specifically argued before the High Court Division that the Subordinate Judge ought to have dismissed the suit on the ground of hardship of the defendant. It appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division considered the question of hardship in extenso and found that the defendant Md Taheruddin Mir entered into a contract with the plaintiff knowing full well that he has only one house at Kishoreganj Town and consequently, the question of hardship of the defendant was rejected by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. The question of hardship is primarily a question of fact and in the present case the learned Judges after proper exercise of their discretion rejected the contention of the defendant and upheld the decree of the trial Court." 

 26. On perusal of the evidences and exhibits it transpires that the claim of hardships could not be raised by both the parties and at the same time if by operation of law the judgment and decree passed by the Courts below is maintained nothing would be left for defendant vendor. 

 Therefore, the leave petition is disposed of. The Judgment and order dated 29-11-2017 passed by the High Court Division is set aside. The suit is dismissed. However, the defendant, is directed to pay solatium of taka 60,00,000 (sixty lac) to the plaintiff including consideration money already paid by the plaintiff within 6(six) months from date, in default, the suit shall stand decreed and the judgment and decree of the trial court shall be restored.
